findings.observation: The CC Application Section 10 indicates the site is subject to Compatibility Standards (checkbox marked 'Yes'). Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan) was examined. The pre-processed blocks.md shows adjacent properties labeled with zoning designations (CS, CS-V, CS-MU-V-CO, SF-3) and land uses. Vision analysis of Sheet 13 confirmed adjacent properties are clearly labeled with zoning (CS, CS-V, CS-MU-V-CO, SF-3) and land uses (USE: OFFICE, USE: APARTMENT/CONDO, USE: COMMERCIAL, USE: GOVERNMENT SERVICES). The SF-3 zoned property to the west is explicitly labeled with text block 'ZONING: SF-3' and 'USE: OFFICE'. Property boundaries are distinctly delineated, and compatibility setback lines are visually shown on the plan adjacent to the SF-3 property.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires a land use map showing adjacent land uses when subject to Compatibility Standards. Compatibility Standards apply per LDC 25-2-1053 because the site is zoned CS-V (less restrictive than MF-4) and is within 75 feet of a triggering property (SF-3 zoned parcel to the west). Sheet 13 provides a comprehensive site plan that functions as the required land use map. It clearly shows property boundaries, adjacent zoning designations for all surrounding properties, and land use labels. The SF-3 triggering property is specifically identified with both zoning and use information. The vision tool confirmed all required elements are visually present and legible. This satisfies the completeness requirement for providing a land use map showing adjacent land uses.

findings.observation: Sheets 35 and 36 were examined for building elevations. Sheet 35 guide.md indicates it contains 'Building elevations for North and East views with material legend.' The blocks.md confirms two elevation drawings (BLDG ELEVATION - NORTH and BLDG ELEVATION - EAST) plus a Material Legend block identifying exterior finishes. Vision analysis of Sheet 35 confirmed both north and east elevations are clearly labeled and shown. The elevations depict comprehensive architectural elements including: building massing and overall design, window/fenestration patterns with a Glazed Opening Schedule table, projecting and inset balconies with glass railings, material finishes shown with varying textures and patterns, and floor levels with specific elevation tags (Level 1 at 0.00 through Roof at 63'-11 1/4"). A Material Legend table is present identifying six exterior finishes: Fiber Cement Board Painted, Metal Panel, King Brick, Wood Tone Fiber Cement, Glass, and Living Wall.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires building elevations showing architectural elements when subject to Compatibility Standards. The site is subject to Compatibility Standards as established for CMP-01. Sheets 35 and 36 provide building elevations for all four sides of the building (North, East, South, West). The vision analysis confirmed these elevations comprehensively show architectural elements including massing, fenestration, balconies, material finishes, and floor levels. A material legend is provided identifying specific exterior finishes. The elevations include floor elevation tags and height indicators. These sheets satisfy the completeness requirement for providing building elevations showing architectural elements. The level of detail is appropriate for a completeness check—detailed adequacy against LDC standards will be assessed during technical review.
findings.explanation: Sheets 35-36 provide building elevations for all four sides showing architectural elements including massing, fenestration, balconies, materials, and floor levels with material legend.

findings.observation: Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 of 2) was examined as it covers the western portion of the site adjacent to the SF-3 triggering property. The guide.md references 'Compatibility Setback Heights' and a 'Compatibility Setback Lines Table' in the key values. The blocks.md confirms Block 3 contains a 'COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINES' table specifying allowable building heights by distance from property line. Vision analysis of Sheet 14 confirmed compatibility setback lines are visually depicted as concentric dashed lines on the plan. These lines are shown adjacent to the SF-3 zoned property to the west, specifically labeled as '15' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', '25' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', '50' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE', and '75' COMPATIBILITY SETBACK LINE'. A Compatibility Setback Lines table is present showing height restrictions: 0'-10' = 0' height (Screening Zone), 10'-25' = 0' height (Restricted Zone), 25'-50' = 40' height, 50'-75' = 60' height. Sheet 13 also shows compatibility setback lines per vision analysis.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires setbacks adjacent to residential uses or zoning to be shown on plans when subject to Compatibility Standards. The site is subject to Compatibility Standards and is adjacent to SF-3 residential zoning to the west. Sheet 14 provides the dimensional control plan for the western portion of the site and clearly shows compatibility setback lines. The vision analysis confirmed these setback lines are visually depicted as dashed concentric lines on the plan (not merely described in a table), are located adjacent to the SF-3 property, and are labeled with specific distances (15', 25', 50', 75'). A table provides the corresponding height restrictions for each setback zone. This visual depiction integrated into the site plan satisfies the completeness requirement. The adequacy of these setbacks against specific LDC 25-2-1051-1063 standards will be assessed during technical review.
findings.explanation: Sheet 14 shows compatibility setback lines (15', 25', 50', 75') visually depicted on plan adjacent to SF-3 residential property with table of height restrictions.
